figures.caption: Figure 1: The temporal-deployment audit at a glance (Octo-Small unless noted [25], n=200). Rows group the story: encoding and the central dissociation (a,b), fallback deployment (c,d), cross-architecture (e,f). (a) Decode R2(t−1) (teal) stays above 0.30 at every depth while the causal deploy gap (rose, occ black − markov, 95% band) is significant only through L4 and collapses at L6. (b) History is decodable (A1) but its unique information (A4, gray) is ≈ 0 in every model and both families: a redundant copy of the present. (c) On the degradation ladder only near-total occlusion (occ black) deploys history; milder degradations are n.s. (d) Interchange (rose) and attention-knockout (plum) both collapse at L6, ruling out a method artifact. (e) Under the same occlusion Octo’s reliance on history rises (fallback) while CronusVLA’s falls (standing), encoding identical (A4≈0 in both). (f) CronusVLA’s contribution is positive when clean, ≈0 under temporal shuffling (order-blind), and falls under occlusion, over three seeds.

Table 1: Positioning: VLA × mechanistic interpretability. Prior work localizes the within-frame modality axis, steers within-frame motion features, or adds memory without a diagnosis; we localize the orthogonal time axis and characterize how history is encoded, deployed, and steered, reaching an architecture-conditional verdict.
Table 16: Per-leg reproduction map (expected headline numbers). All legs read the same frozen, hashed stimulus set; runs are on one consumer GPU with frozen public checkpoints.

Figure 4: Population and behavioral evidence (Octo-Small [25]). (a) Mean per-DoF |∆| under masking vs. swapping t−1: history influences the continuous pose dimensions throughout, not just the gripper. (b) Per-pair lost fraction of the frame across the frozen set; the distribution sits far below the near-total-occlusion band that triggers deployment, so only 3/250 pairs are naturally occluded, the fallback is seldom triggered in distribution.

Figure 3: Supporting panels (Octo-Small unless noted [25]): (a) decode by depth, (b) per-layer interchange contribution, (c) five-seed deploy-gap hardening with a permutation test, (d) inverse scaling across model size. These expand the summary panels of Figure 1.
